ABANDONING CHILD
Cornwall, ON – A 25-year-old woman from Cornwall was arrested on May 8, 2026, and charged with abandoning child. On the evening of May 7, 2026, members of the Cornwall Police Service were dispatched to a Pitt Street establishment to investigate a report of a child allegedly left unattended inside a motor vehicle. The investigation revealed the woman unlawfully abandoned her child and acted in a manner that was likely to endanger the child’s life. As a result of the investigation, reasonable and probable grounds were developed for her arrest. On May 8, 2026, the woman was located, taken into custody and charged accordingly. She was later released to appear in court on June 16, 2026. The child was assessed by paramedics and did not sustain physical injuries.

A warrant was issued for the individual’s arrest on the charge of failure to attend court after having appeared. On May 8, 2026, police responded to a disturbance, and an investigation ensued. The youth was located, the warrant was executed and they were held for a bail hearing.

title: Media Release - Cornwall Police Service Board Announces New Chief Designate
content:
Cornwall Police Service Board Announces new Chief Designate
Cornwall, ON – Cornwall Police Service Board is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Hugh Stevenson as the new Chief Designate until Chief Shawna Spowart’s official retirement at the end of 2026. Mr. Stevenson will then become the Chief of the Cornwall Police Service (CPS) as of January 1, 2027.
“We are quite excited that Mr. Stevenson will be joining our team. He brings a wealth of knowledge and experience. He is a transformational policing executive with 38 years of leadership across both municipal and provincial policing,” said Chair Brisson. “Most recently he has served as Chief of Police for the Sault Ste. Marie Police Service (2018–2025)—a municipal service comparable to the Cornwall Police Service in its resource constraints, staffing pressures, and border-related demands. He fully understands the importance of being present and engaged in the community and as such will be relocating to Cornwall or the surrounding area within the next few weeks. We look forward to our new partnership with Mr. Stevenson.” He will be officially sworn in at the June 25, 2026, CPS Board meeting.
Hugh Stevenson: “My experience, leadership, and proven results as a municipal Chief of Police and Senior OPP Executive align directly with Cornwall’s stated requirements. I bring a demonstrated record of building respectful, high-functioning partnerships with all stakeholders. I am prepared to lead the Cornwall Police Service in true partnership with the Board and all civilian and sworn members, fostering a culture of trust, accountability, and collaboration while advancing forward-thinking, evidence-based policing strategies. I am ready to deliver the leadership required to strengthen public confidence and ensure the continued safety, resilience, and long-term prosperity of Cornwall and its residents.”
His leadership is anchored in transparent communication, strong governance, and a collaborative partnership with the Police Service Board, ensuring alignment on strategic priorities, fiscal accountability, and organizational integrity. He brings expertise in governance, fiscal stewardship, research, and strategic planning, complemented by a sustained commitment to people development—mentoring, empowering, and preparing both sworn and civilian members to become the next generation of leaders.
His career reflects a sustained commitment to continuous professional development, both personally and in fostering a culture of learning among peers and subordinates. He holds advanced academic credentials, including a Bachelor of Arts in Criminology (Law and Psychology) from Carleton University, a master’s degree in criminology from the University of Toronto and a Doctorate in Education (Clinical Psychology and Teaching) from the University of Toronto. Most recently, he completed the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) course in Artificial Intelligence and Business Strategy further strengthening his capacity to lead in an increasingly technology-driven policing environment.

title: CPS WARNS OF INCREASE IN VEHICLE, TRAILER AND WATERCRAFT THEFTS
content:
CPS WARNS OF INCREASE IN VEHICLE, TRAILER AND WATERCRAFT THEFTS
CPS WARNS OF INCREASE IN VEHICLE, TRAILER AND WATERCRAFT THEFTS
CORNWALL – The Cornwall Police Service (CPS), in partnership with Équité Association, is raising awareness about a growing trend in thefts involving not only motor vehicles, but also recreational property such as trailers, boats and personal watercraft.
While auto theft remains a concern across Eastern Ontario, the CPS has also seen incidents involving the theft of recreational trailers, ATVs, boats and Sea-Doos. These items are often targeted due to their high value, ease of transport and, in many cases, lack of security measures.
Through continued collaboration with Équité Association – a national not-for-profit supporting Canadian insurers in the fight against fraud – the CPS is working to identify trends, support investigations and promote prevention strategies to reduce these crimes and their connection to organized criminal activity.
“Property theft, including vehicles and recreational equipment, is not a crime of opportunity alone – it is often tied to larger networks,” said S/Sgt. Scott Bonneville. “By working with partners like Équité and engaging the public, we can better protect our community and reduce the risk of victimization.”
As part of ongoing prevention efforts, the CPS is reminding residents to follow the principles of the LOCK IT OR LOSE IT campaign and take a layered approach to security.
CRIME PREVENTION TIPS:
Always lock vehicles, trailers and storage compartments when not in use
Park in well-lit areas or inside a secured garage whenever possible
Use hitch locks, wheel clamps or trailer locks for recreational equipment
Store boats and Sea-Doos in secured areas and remove keys when unattended
Install GPS tracking devices on high-value property
Position trailers or equipment in a way that makes removal difficult (e.g., blocked in)
Install motion lighting and surveillance cameras at home or storage locations
Avoid leaving ownership documents or valuables inside vehicles or trailers
Remain vigilant – thieves may return to target replacement property
Residents are encouraged to report suspicious activity immediately
Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) footage also continues to play a critical role in these investigations. As part of ongoing prevention efforts, the CPS encourages residents and business owners to support community safety by participating in the CamSafe program.
CamSafe is a voluntary CCTV and security video registry that allows community members to register their surveillance cameras, helping officers quickly identify potential video sources when investigating incidents in the area.
CAMSAFE
: https://cornwallpolice.com/en/record-services/services.html/security-camera-registry
Community awareness and vigilance remain key in preventing theft and protecting property.
For non-emergencies, please contact the CPS at 613-932-2110. To report a crime in progress, call 9-1-1.

title: Animal Cruelty Investigation Under PAWS Review
content:
Animal Cruelty Investigation Under PAWS Review
Cornwall, ON - Cornwall Police Service (CPS) initiated an investigation on Tuesday, April 14, following a complaint received regarding a video circulating on social media depicting animal cruelty. The CPS was subsequently in communication with Provincial Animal Welfare Services (PAWS).
The Ontario Provincial Animal Welfare Services Act mandates a government-run enforcement model to protect animals from abuse and neglect. It authorizes inspectors to enforce animal care standards, investigate complaints, and impose Canada's highest penalties for welfare violations.
As such, PAWS has taken carriage of the investigation and the CPS will be updated accordingly.
Members of the public are reminded not to take matters into their own hands and to allow the appropriate authorities to conduct a thorough investigation.
PAWS MANDATE
Enforcement & Accountability: Operates a 24/7 hotline (1-833-9-ANIMAL) and employs specialized inspectors to enforce provincial standards of care.
Stricter Penalties: Imposes severe penalties for animal cruelty, including substantial fines and imprisonment for up to two years.
PAWS ACT
: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/19p13

title: WOMAN CHARGED IN CONNECTION TO STABBING
content:
WOMAN CHARGED IN CONNECTION TO STABBING
WOMAN CHARGED IN CONNECTION TO STABBING
Cornwall, ON – A 35-year-old woman from Cornwall was arrested on March 12, 2026, on the strength of an outstanding warrant.
At approximately 8 p.m. on Feb. 28, 2026, members of the Cornwall Police Service responded to a stabbing in the area of First Street East and Prince Arthur Street. An extensive investigation ensued, led by the Criminal Investigation Division.
It is alleged on Feb. 28, 2026, the woman was in possession of an edged weapon, contrary to her prohibition order, and stabbed an individual. The man sustained life-threatening injuries and was rushed to hospital.
As a result of the investigation, a warrant was subsequently issued for the woman’s arrest on the charges of:
Aggravated assault
Possession of a weapon for dangerous purpose
Possession of a firearm or ammunition contrary to prohibition order
On March 12, 2026, members of the Ontario Provincial Police’s Repeat Offender Parole Enforcement (ROPE) squad, with assistance from the CPS’ Criminal Investigation Division, located the woman.
The warrant was executed, and she was held for a bail hearing.
Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) footage played a key role in the investigation. As the CPS continues to investigate incidents, residents and business owners are encouraged to take advantage of the CamSafe program.
CamSafe is a voluntary CCTV and security video registry that allows community members to register their surveillance cameras, helping officers quickly identify potential video sources when investigating crimes in the area.

title: MAN CHARGED FOLLOWING HATE-MOTIVATED INVESTIGATION
content:
MAN CHARGED FOLLOWING HATE-MOTIVATED INVESTIGATION
MAN CHARGED FOLLOWING HATE-MOTIVATED INVESTIGATION
Cornwall, ON – The Cornwall Police Service (CPS) has arrested a 19-year-old man from Cornwall in connection with a hate-motivated investigation involving threatening online behaviour.
The individual is charged with two counts of uttering threats to cause death or bodily harm and two counts of criminal harassment related to threatening conduct.
On Dec. 18, 2025, a hate crime detective with the Criminal Investigation Division began investigating a series of social media posts. The investigation determined that between Nov. 3 and Dec. 15, 2025, the accused allegedly made threatening statements and engaged in threatening behaviour directed toward members of the Jewish and Black communities.
As a result of the investigation, police developed reasonable and probable grounds for the man’s arrest. On Jan. 29, 2026, the accused was taken into custody, charged accordingly and held for a bail hearing.
“Hate-motivated behaviour, including threats made online, causes real and lasting harm,” said Inspector Tracey Pilon. “These acts create fear, divide communities and undermine the sense of safety that everyone deserves.”
“The Cornwall Police Service takes these incidents very seriously and will continue to investigate them thoroughly.”
Police are emphasizing the importance of reporting hate crimes and hate incidents. Even when conduct does not meet the threshold of a criminal offence, reporting helps police understand the scope and impact of hate-related activity in the community and supports prevention efforts.
“We want residents to know there are accessible and confidential ways to report hate crimes and hate incidents,” said Insp. Pilon. “Coming forward helps protect individuals, strengthens community trust and sends a clear message that hate has no place in the City of Cornwall.”
Anyone wishing to report a hate crime or hate incident is encouraged to visit the CPS website at: https://cornwallpolice.com/en/crime-prevention/crime-prevention.html/hate-motivated-incidents
WHAT IS A HATE CRIME?
A hate crime is a criminal offence committed against a person or property motivated in whole or in part by the offender’s (real or perceived) bias, prejudice or hate against an identifiable group (such as, race, nationality, ethnicity, language, colour, religion, gender expression or identity, age, mental or physical disability or sexual orientation or similar factor). Examples include assault, mischief (graffiti), and uttering threats, etc.
WHAT IS A HATE INCIDENT?
A hate/bias incident is a non-criminal action or behaviour that is motivated by hate against an identifiable group. Examples include, “Go back to your country”, racial slurs or other derogatory remarks about being part of an identifiable group, etc.

title: CPS RETIREMENT & APPRECIATION EVENING
content:
CPS RETIREMENT & APPRECIATION EVENING
Cornwall, ON – On the evening of Thursday, May 21, 2026, the Cornwall Police Service (CPS), Cornwall Police Association (CPA) and Senior Officers’ Association (SOA) held its annual Retirement & Appreciation Evening at the DEV Hotel & Conference Centre.
City of Cornwall Mayor Justin Towndale, MP Eric Duncan and CPS Board Chair Amanda Brisson were in attendance for the event.
Ms Diane Fortin, Cst. Andrew Arbic, Cst. Sherri Camerson and Ms Helene Parthenais were recognized in celebration of their retirement.
Ms Fortin joined the CPS in 2008 as a Communications Dispatcher and became Supervisor of the Communications Bureau in 2009, a role she held until her retirement on Dec. 30, 2025. Ms Fortin is known for her steady leadership and strong advocacy on behalf of Communications members.
Cst. Andrew Arbic began his career with the CPS in 1999 as a constable in Community Patrol. He transferred to Crime Reduction & Community Partnerships (CRCP) in 2005 and served within the Criminal Investigation Division (CID) during his career. In 2011, he returned to CRCP, remaining there until 2022 when he rejoined Community Patrol, where he served until his retirement. Cst. Arbic retired from the Service on Dec. 31, 2025. Throughout his career, he developed strong relationships with youth and worked closely with a wide range of community partners.
Cst. Cameron joined the CPS in 1995 as a Community Patrol constable, later transferring to CID in 1999 and CRCP in 2005. In 2010, she moved to the Sexual Assault and Child Abuse (SACA) Unit before returning to CRCP in 2018, where she spearheaded the Vulnerable Sector Mobile Acute Response Team (VSMART). She retired from the Service on Jan. 31, 2026. Throughout her career, Cst. Cameron built strong community partnerships and was widely recognized for her dedicated victim advocacy, particularly for those in the vulnerable sector.
Ms Parthenais joined the CPS in 2008 as a Data Input Clerk in the Records Bureau. Throughout her career, she also served as a coach officer, mentoring and supporting new employees as they entered the Service. She retired from the Service on Feb. 28, 2026, after 18 years of dedicated service to the community. Ms Parthenais is recognized for her strong work ethic and her commitment to guiding and supporting new staff.
.
CHIEF SPOWART HONOURED
Chief Spowart was presented with a CPS Long Service Award recognizing 30 years of dedicated service. Throughout her career, she has served in Community Patrol, CID and Executive Services, rising through the ranks to Sergeant in 2007, Staff Sergeant in 2013, Inspector in 2014, Deputy Chief in 2018 and Chief in 2021.
She was also recently honoured with the Ontario Women in Law Enforcement (OWLE) Heritage Award, recognizing her leadership, mentorship and contributions to advancing women in policing. In addition, Chief Spowart received the Police Exemplary Service Medal, 30-year first bar, awarded for exemplary service characterized by good conduct, industry and efficiency.
PEER APPRECIATION AWARDS
The 3rd annual Peer-to-Peer Appreciation awards were presented.
The Difference Maker Award and the Leadership Award were selected based on nominations and voting by CPS employees. These awards provided employees the opportunity to show their appreciation for colleagues’ dedication, leadership and making a difference each day at the CPS.
Cst. Raheem Aman was the recipient of the Difference Maker Award for 2025.
Cst. Aman consistently goes above and beyond his regular duties, demonstrating strong leadership, positivity and commitment within the CPS and the broader community.
He is known for his upbeat attitude and supportive approach, fostering a positive workplace culture where colleagues feel valued and encouraged. His willingness to assist others and lead by example makes him a key source of positivity within the CPS.
In the community, Cst. Aman actively mentors youth and supports initiatives that promote engagement, growth and positive relationships with policing. His contributions have had a meaningful and lasting impact.
Cst. Aman’s dedication and influence reflect the spirit of the Difference Maker Award, making him a valued representative of the CPS both professionally and personally.
Also nominated for the award were Cst. Pat Huygen, D/Cst. Justin Lafleur, Sp/Cst. Tasha Mallette and Sp/Cst. Meg Sommerville.
Sgt. Matthew Lemire was the recipient of the Leadership Award for 2025.
Sgt. Lemire’s leadership in the Court Bureau has been highly effective, bringing the team together into a cohesive, collaborative unit built on trust and shared purpose. He consistently leads with positivity, calmness and a strong example.
He is always willing to step in and support his team, whether in daily operations or broader organizational initiatives, helping to strengthen morale and reinforce a culture of teamwork and optimism. Colleagues rely on him for encouragement, guidance and practical assistance.
As a communicator, Sgt. Lemire is inclusive and intentional, ensuring the right voices are involved in decision-making to support informed and sustainable outcomes.
As Court Supervisor, he represents the CPS with professionalism and integrity in all interactions with the public, the Crown’s Office, and the Ministry of the Attorney General. His leadership and steady influence make him a strong and deserving recipient of this peer award.
Also nominated for the award were S/Sgt. Scott Bonneville and Cst. Rod Degray.
The CPS would like to congratulate all of the recipients on their incredible achievements and continued dedication to serving the City of Cornwall.

title: CPS, CITY PARTNERS COMPLETE SUCCESSFUL SPRING CLEAN UP PILOT PROJECT
content:
Cornwall, ON – The City of Cornwall has successfully completed its inaugural Spring Clean Up pilot project, a collaborative initiative aimed at improving neighbourhood safety, property standards and community well-being through education, engagement and partnership.
The week-long campaign, which was held June 8-12, 2026, brought together staff from the Cornwall Police Service (CPS), Cornwall Fire Services, Cornwall By-Law Services and Cornwall Waste Management Services. Working in multidisciplinary teams, members visited pre-identified neighbourhoods to engage with residents, address concerns and provide information on crime prevention, fire safety, property maintenance and proper waste disposal.
Rather than focusing solely on enforcement, the initiative emphasized education, support and connecting residents with the appropriate resources available through City services.
“Throughout the week, teams visited 536 residences, engaged directly with 298 residents, and identified 149 follow-up actions requiring further attention from one or more participating departments,” said Sgt. Dave MacLean, head of the CPS Crime Reduction & Community Partnerships (CRCP) division.
Recognizing that some concerns may be linked to mental health challenges, the CPS Mobile Crisis Response Team (MCRT) also participated throughout the initiative, providing assistance and connecting individuals with appropriate supports when needed.
Residents received educational materials covering a variety of topics, including:
Crime prevention information such as Lock It or Lose It and CamSafe
Fire safety education, including smoke alarm awareness, safe smoking practices and barbecue safety
Property standards and landlord and tenant responsibilities
Waste sorting, recycling and proper disposal resources
The project also encouraged community participation beyond City services. Community organizations, including the Renaissance Group, coordinated neighbourhood clean-up efforts in parks, trails and public spaces, while local schools participated in community clean-up initiatives through the City's Adopt-a-Street program. Students from St. Matthew Catholic Secondary School and St. Lawrence Secondary School completed clean-up projects in Lamoureux Park and Kinsmen Park, respectively.
Daily briefings and debriefings allowed participating departments to coordinate efforts, share information and identify emerging concerns. Team members also reported overwhelmingly positive interactions with residents and noted the value of working alongside colleagues from other City departments to better understand each service’s role in supporting the community.
“The success of the Spring Clean-Up initiative is a direct result of strong collaboration between our Police, By-Law, Fire Services, and Environmental Services teams,” said Deputy Chief/Manager By-Law Services, Leighton Woods. “By working together, we were able to deliver a coordinated and proactive approach that made a meaningful impact in our community.”

title: CPS CONDUCTS TAXI SAFETY INITIATIVE
content:
Cornwall, ON – The Cornwall Police Service (CPS) recently conducted a coordinated taxi inspection initiative aimed at enhancing public safety and ensuring compliance with provincial legislation and municipal regulations governing commercial passenger transportation.
Officers focused on vehicle safety, driver documentation, licensing requirements, and overall compliance to help ensure that residents and visitors can rely on safe and properly regulated transportation services.
This initiative reflects the CPS’ ongoing commitment to enhancing community safety through proactive enforcement, strong partnerships and collaborative problem-solving. By working together, our members continue to achieve meaningful outcomes that directly benefit the public while supporting the Service’s organizational priorities.
“We are committed to taking a proactive approach to traffic and public safety,” said S/Sgt. George Knezevic. “Initiatives such as these demonstrate the value of collaboration and our dedication to ensuring commercial passenger vehicles operating in our community meet the required safety and regulatory standards.”
The CPS will continue to conduct targeted traffic safety and compliance initiatives throughout the year as part of its ongoing efforts to improve road safety and strengthen public confidence.

title: CPS charges man following e-bike investigation
content:
Cornwall, ON – One individual has been arrested and charged following an investigation into the dangerous operation of an electric dirt bike throughout the city.
In recent weeks, the Cornwall Police Service received multiple complaints regarding individuals allegedly operating electric dirt bikes in a dangerous manner on city streets, sidewalks, crosswalks and private property. Reported behaviours included performing stunts, travelling at high speeds in pedestrian areas and creating a risk to public safety.
As a result of an investigation by the CPS Traffic Unit, officers located and arrested one of the individuals involved. Investigators utilized a variety of investigative techniques, including drone technology, to gather evidence and assist with the investigation.
On Aug. 5, 2026, a 21-year-old man from Cornwall was arrested and charged with dangerous operation, contrary to the Criminal Code of Canada, as well as several Highway Traffic Act violations:
Drive motor vehicle – perform stunt
Drive motor vehicle – improper licence
Owner operate motor vehicle – no insurance
Novice driver – fail to surrender licence
Unlawfully drive an off-road vehicle on a highway
Failure to notify change of address
Drive motor vehicle – no plates
Drive motor vehicle – no permit
The man was taken into custody, charged accordingly and later released to appear in court on Sept. 8, 2026.
Police have also developed reasonable and probable grounds for the arrest of two additional individuals.
“Our community has seen an increase in complaints regarding off-road vehicles being operated on city streets and cyclists and e-bike riders failing to obey traffic laws, creating a serious public and road safety concern,” said Deputy Chief Chad Maxwell. “Every person using our roads, regardless of their mode of transportation, has a responsibility to follow the rules designed to protect all road users, as ignoring traffic laws increases the risk of collisions, injuries, and tragic outcomes for everyone, including pedestrians, motorists, cyclists and families in our neighbourhoods.”
The CPS reminds the public that electric dirt bikes and off-road vehicles are subject to provincial legislation. These vehicles are generally prohibited from operating on municipal roads, sidewalks, parks and other public areas unless specifically authorized by law. Individuals who choose to operate these vehicles illegally may face criminal and provincial charges, vehicle seizures and significant fines.
“The vast majority of road users act responsibly, but a small number of individuals continue to operate in a manner that puts themselves and others at risk,” said Deputy Chief Maxwell. “Our officers will continue balancing education and enforcement efforts to address unlawful off-road vehicle use and dangerous cycling and e-bike behaviours.”
The message is simple: If you choose to use our roadways, you must do so safely and lawfully.
“Our goal is not enforcement for the sake of enforcement, but safer streets, fewer collisions and greater protection for everyone who lives, works and travels in the City of Cornwall,” said Deputy Chief Maxwell.
The investigation remains ongoing as police continue working to identify and arrest two additional individuals involved. Anyone with information that could assist police is asked to contact the CPS at 613-933-5000, ext. 3. You may also share information anonymously by contacting Seaway Valley Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

title: Media Release - Aug. 20, 2026
content:
FAIL TO COMPLY, THEFT OF MOTOR VEHICLE
Cornwall, ON – A 37-year-old man from Cornwall was arrested on Aug. 19, 2026, and charged with two counts of fail to comply with probation order and one count of theft of motor vehicle. On Aug. 3, 2026, a Cornwall Police Service officer was dispatched to investigate a theft of motor vehicle complaint. It is alleged on this date, the man was bound by two separate probation orders, each with the relevant condition to keep the peace and be of good behaviour. It is further alleged he stole his spouse’s motor vehicle. As a result of the investigation, police developed reasonable and probable grounds for his arrest. On Aug. 19, 2026, the man attended police headquarters to address the matter. He was taken into custody, charged accordingly and later released to appear in court on Sept. 8, 2026.
POSSESSION OF FIREARM CONTRARY TO PROHIBITION ORDER, UNAUTHORIZED POSSESSION OF WEAPON, CARRYING CONCEALED WEAPON
Cornwall, ON – A 68-year-old man from Akwesasne was arrested on Aug. 19, 2026, and charged with the following:
Possession of a firearm or ammunition contrary to prohibition order
Unauthorized possession of a weapon
Carrying a concealed weapon
On Aug. 19, 2026, a CPS officer was dispatched to the Port of Entry, where a Canada Border Services Agency officer had a man in custody. It is alleged on this date, the man was bound by a weapons prohibition order and was in possession of a taser. He was subsequently turned over to the CPS, where he was charged accordingly. The man was later released to appear in court on Sept. 22, 2026.
FAIL TO COMPLY, SHOPLIFTING
Cornwall, ON – A 57-year-old man from Cornwall was arrested on Aug. 20, 2026, on the strength of an outstanding warrant. It is alleged on April 17, 2026, the man was bound by a probation order with the relevant conditions to keep the peace and be of good behaviour and to not attend a specific Ninth Street West business. It is further alleged on this date, the man attended the Ninth Street West business he was prohibited from visiting, selected merchandise and exited the store without making any attempt to pay for the items. Police were contacted and an investigation ensued – led by a Community Safety Officer. A warrant was subsequently issued for his arrest on the charges of two counts of fail to comply with probation order and one count of theft under $5,000 – shoplifting. In the early morning hours of Aug. 20, 2026, police were dispatched to a suspicious person complaint, and an investigation ensued. The man was located and taken into custody. The warrant was executed and he was later released to appear in court on Sept. 24, 2026.
